articleTitle: A Compact and Simple Prototype CPW-Fed Dual Band Antenna for ISM, Wi-Fi, and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, geometrically simple, and low profile CPW fed dual-band antenna is proposed for ISM, WLAN, and Wi-Fi applications. The proposed antenna is embedded on substrate material Roger/RT 5870 with a thickness of 0.79 mm. The overall size antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{23 \text{mm} \times 32 \text{mm}}$</tex>. The proposed design consists of a rectangular monopole radiator with a CPW feed line along with slots and two stubs at the top and bottom of the rectangular radiator to improve the performance of the antenna. The antenna is designed and analyzed by using the software tool HFSS (High Frequency Solution Simulator).

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Microstrip Patch Antenna Design: Observations and Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, the relationship between the configuration parameters of microstrip patch antenna and its resonant frequency is analyzed from the machine learning aspect. By training two datasets with 258 and 4209 antenna configurations, the linear regression model shows that the mean value of resonant frequency accuracy prediction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{R^{2}}$</tex> score achieves 0.582 and 0.647 under 3 times of repeated 5-fold cross-validations for the operational frequency range from 3 to 15 GHz. Larger datasets with higher prediction accuracy would make the machine-learning-based model a potential method in antenna design without the need for massive dimensional tuning in full-wave simulators for this type of patch antenna.

articleTitle: A Compact Unit-cell Design for mmWave Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact unit-cell design for 1-bit reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) with suppressed quantization lobes. This is achieved by introducing a random pre-phasing over the RIS., utilizing delay lines within the confined space of the unit-cell. To achieve a compact topology with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda/2}$</tex> unit cell periodicity., a triple-layer stack-up topology is presented. As such., the unit cell comprises., a patch antenna., a delay line., a radio-frequency (RF) choke., a Vcc pad., and a PIN diode switch within a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{5\text{mm}\times 5\text{mm}}$</tex> footprint. We evaluate the proposed unit cell layout with full-wave simulations of a 64-element tile at 28 GHz. The presented RIS topology could be leveraged to extend the signal coverage., increase signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), or improve physical layer security (PLS) in mm Wave 5G and beyond wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband MIMO Antenna Realization for Indoor Ka-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, two port multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna is presented for Ka-band 5G communication system. The proposed design is embedded over substrate material Roger RT/duroid 5870 with unit element size of 8 mm ×8 mm × 0.79 mm. The geometrical simple, compact, ultra-wide band and high gain makes the proposed design a potential candidate for future wireless indoor devices. Moreover, a two port MIMO antenna was designed using the unit element for MIMO applications. Furthermore, various performance parameters of the proposed MIMO antenna were analyzed by using EM simulation tool Ansoft HFSS (High Frequency Solution Simulator) and compared with related work to show the potential of proposed work

articleTitle: Ultra-Lightweight Transmitarray Antenna Enabled by Charge-Programmed Three-Dimensional Multi-Material Printing
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We for the first time introduce charge-programmed three-dimensional (3D) multi-material printing to large-aperture antenna fabrication, and present the development of a circularly-polarized, ultra-lightweight transmitarray antenna at 19 GHz. This transmitarray contains three layers of metallic patterns spaced by dielectric supporting structures. This entire antenna is manufactured in a single-step process, in contrast to the traditional methods using printed circuit board process which requires alignment and bonding of multiple layers. Significant weight reduction in the antenna is achieved by selectively printing the supporting dielectric material. The 12-cm-diameter transmi-tarray weighs only 5 g, which can be an order of magnitude reduction compared to one based on common laminate.

articleTitle: A 90-125 GHz Stacked PA in 130 nm InP HBT with 18.3 % peak PAE at 15.3 dBm Output Power
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband stacked power amplifier implemented in a 130 nm InP HBT process. The phase of the load lines at the two stages are aligned using an interstage matching network to maximize output power. The peak DC power consumption is 160 mW. The amplifier achieves a peak gain of 11.5 dB and a 3 dB bandwidth greater than 50 GHz, measured from 90 GHz to 140 GHz with a peak PAE and output power at 112.5 GHz of 18.3 % and 15.3 dBm respectively. This design demonstrates the viability of the stacked PA topology in improving power output in amplifiers designed in process nodes with low breakdown voltages.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Interference Detection in Microwave Radiometry Using Bayesian Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Herein, a probabilistic approach is proposed to detect and mitigate radio frequency interference (RFI) in mi-crowave radiometer measurements. Simulated RFI-free and RFI-contaminated radiometer measurements are analyzed at the feature level while considering their probability density functions. For each measurement, the features are reviewed sequentially. The final decision is made based on maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. The proposed framework is evaluated using monte-carlo simulations. The comparison with the existing RFI detection techniques through numerical simulations demonstrates the ability of the proposed approach to detect RFI even when the interference to noise (INR) of the RFI is as low as −15 dB.

articleTitle: RFSoC-Based Digital Beamformer for Millimeter-Wave MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel 4-channel digital beam-forming receiver architecture for 5G millimeter-Wave cellular communications. The receiver is based on a code-multiplexed topology where all the channels are encoded with unique or-thogonal Walsh-Hadamard codes and multiplexed into a single-channel. A single wideband analog-to-digital converter (ADC) on RF-SoC FPGA is employed at the digital back-end which significantly reduces the cost, complexity and power consumption of the hardware realization. The digital signal processor (DSP) algorithms for multi-channel synchronization and beamforming are implemented on the Xilinx ZCU111 RF-SoC FPGA proto-typing platform. An end - to-end measurement setup including ultrawideband antenna array (TCDA), a custom-designed and fabricated Encoder Circuit Board (ECB) and FPGA processor are also included for system validation. A maximum clock frequency of 400 MHz was used for generation of the unique codes and decoding the desired signals at the receiver end. To the best of the author's knowledge a maximum of 36 dB interchannel interference ratio (ICI) was achieved which is the highest to be reported in literature till dates.

articleTitle: Doppler Frequency Shift Compensation in Millimeter-Wave Multi-Port Receiver Front-Ends
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, a carrier recovery system is proposed to precisely estimate and compensate for the Doppler shift in millimeter-wave multi-port receivers. It includes the frequency and phase correction units in two parallel paths. These paths are loops close after demodulation and have an impact on each other's output. The proposed system accurately finds and compensates for the Doppler shift in the received signals up to 11 kHz.

articleTitle: Solving Full Waveform Inversion Enhanced by Efficient Progressive Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The full waveform inversion (FWI) is highly non-linear and underdetermined. Due to the limitation of acquisition devices, low-frequency information may be missing from obtained data. The absence of low-frequency information could severely compromise FWI results. To solve these problems, we propose a learning-based approach to extrapolate the low-frequency data using a progressive transfer learning workflow to eliminate the labeling requirement for training. The system is implemented on a differentiable program platform to take advantage of automatic differentiation. The performance of the system is validated by an electromagnetic (EM) inverse problem. Our experiment results show that the proposed method is efficient and effective.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Heart Rate Estimation in Low SNR Environments Using mmWave Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Extracting accurate heart rate estimates of human subjects from a distance in high-noise scenarios using radar is a common problem. Often, frequency components from sources such as movement and vital signs from other subjects can overpower the weak reflected signal of the heart. In this study, we propose a signal processing scheme using an Adaptive Multi-Trace Carving algorithm (AMTC) to accurately detect the heart rate signal over time in non-ideal scenarios using a mm-wave radar. In our initial proof-of-concept results, we show a low heart rate estimation mean absolute error (MAE) of 3bpm for a single subject marching in place and less than 4.5bpm for a scenario of two human subjects at the same distance from the radar.

articleTitle: Low Sidelobe Level Randomized Reconfigurable Reflective Surfaces under Oblique Incidence
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We present a pre-quantization technique to simplify the design of a randomized reconfigurable reflective surface (RRS). Randomized RRSs offer the advantage of suppressing the parasitic quantization lobes that plague the reflective surface designs employing plane wave illumination. The randomization is implemented using random but fixed phase delay structures in the unit cell of each radiating element. This paper provides a set of guidelines for choosing the smallest number of such randomized phase delays to achieve the desired sidelobe level. As such, adopting the technique presented in this work, it is possible to minimize the number of unique phase delay structures required to design a randomized RRS, thereby reducing design and fabrication complexities.

articleTitle: Mechanically Configurable, Capacitively Coupled, Disk Loaded Monopole Driven Corner Reflector
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a disc loaded monopole that is mechanically configurable for both the 2.3 GHz amateur radio band and 2.45 GHz Wi-Fi, The antenna is designed to be weather and heat resistant for outdoor use and requires no direct electrical contact for mechanical tuning. The simulated results were given for both the ideal configuration in air, and the resin embedded antenna.

articleTitle: A Particle Swarm Approach to Grating Lobe Suppression in an Aperiodic Vivaldi Array
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: To avoid grating lobes, periodic array elements must be λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>/2 apart. For wideband arrays, sparsity in array element sparsity is unavoidable. This paper explores using particle swarm optimization to create an aperiodic spacing between Vivaldi elements to help suppress grating lobes from 2–40 GHz.

articleTitle: Low Noise L-band RF-over-fiber Signal Transport for ALPACA on the GBT
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: After the catastrophic failure of the Arecibo Tele-scope on Dec. 1, 2020, the intended host telescope for the 69-element wide-field phased array feed ALPACA instrument was lost. Design of the RF -over-fiber (RFoF) signal transport link to the FPGA/GPU digital beamformer back end was revisited to accommodate the physical and operating requirements of a new host telescope. The equivalent noise temperature of the link must be below 850 K in order for signal transport to contribute no more than 1 K to the target system noise temperature performance of 27 K for the instrument. We present progress of the new design and report on its performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Wearable Joint Flexion Sensor Using Anatomical Tissue Models
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Joint flexion monitoring is critical to applications as diverse as healthcare, sports, gaming, etc. Nevertheless, existing technologies used to monitor joint kinematics are either restricted to contrived lab environments or lack liability and accuracy. We previously reported a wrap-around wearable loop sensor that overcomes these limitations. To date, the design has only been studied using cylindrical models to emulate the limb. In this work, we employ an anatomical arm model to further validate the design. Simulation results confirm that the sensor can reliably detect elbow flexion angles in the typical range of motion (i.e., 0°-130°). In the future, the design can be integrated into garments for seamless, real-world monitoring of joint flexion.

articleTitle: Toward Fully Biodegradable and Renewable Antennas Using 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents two of the first fully 3D-printed antennas based on 100% biodegradable and renewable host substrates for the next generation of wireless communication systems. To understand the electromagnetic properties of the biodegradable materials, their complex permittivities are mea-sured across an ultra-wide frequency range from 200 MHz to 20 GHz, using a Keysight 85070E Performance Probe. To verify the concept, dipole antennas with embedded conductive parts are designed and fabricated using the characterized materials through 3D printing technology. The host substrate of the antennas are made of the BioFila silk and linen filaments. The conductive parts of the antennas are fabricated using 3D-printed graphene. The reflection coefficient and radiation patterns of the fabricated antennas are measured, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Far Field EVM Estimation for Large Phased Arrays using Embedded Elements and Beam Squint Model
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The use of narrowband RF phase shifters in phased arrays produces beam squint, wherein the main beam direction shifts away from the direction used to establish a phase gradient for the array elements at the center frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\mathrm{c}}$</tex>. The resulting frequency-dependent amplitude distortion can degrade the EVM of wideband modulated signals if uncompensated in the receiver equalizer. Error vector magnitude (EVM), the root-mean-square value of the difference between transmitted and received symbols in the complex plane, is simulated for a 16-QAM test signal using a MATLAB model for the phased array signal transmission and full-wave simulations of the embedded element far field patterns at each scan angle in order to demonstrate the beam squint effect in conjunction with the array element bandwidth characteristic. The results show that the element bandwidth can either enhance or reduce the linear distortion caused by the beam squint effect.

articleTitle: The Design and SAR Analysis of a UWB Bow-tie Antenna for Wireless Wearable Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents design of a wearable flexible patch antenna and its corresponding SAR (specific absorption rate) analysis when placed on a human body. The substrate material used is polyimide with a thickness of 0.1 mm, and gold is used for the patch and ground material with 200 nm thickness. The di-electric constant and the tangent loss of the polyimide substrate are 3.5 and 0.0002, respectively. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\times 30\times 0.1004 \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The designed antenna has the resonating frequency at 3.45 GHz and a bandwidth of 2.6 GHz. The far field gain of the designed antenna is 7.5 dBi. The SAR analysis generated an SAR value of 0.174 W/kg, which is within the safe limit of 2W/kg averaged over 10g of tissue as specified by the ICNIRP (International Commission of Non-Ionization Radiation Protection). This suggests that the designed antenna is safe and can be utilized for wireless wearable sensors.

articleTitle: On the Far-Field Characteristics of a 3D-printed Antenna Using Wood-Based PLA and Conductive Silver Nanoparticle Ink
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper reports the far-filed characteristics of a class of 3D-printed dipole antenna fabricated using wood-based polylactic acid (PLA). The electromagnetic properties (dielectric constant and dielectric loss factor) of the wood-based PLA are measured from 200 MHz to 20 GHz, using a Keysight 85070E Performance dielectric Probe, and its loss tangents values (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tan}\ \delta$</tex>) are calculated accordingly. The conductive parts of the antenna are fabricated using silver nanoparticle ink. The antenna is fabricated using a desktop 3D printer. The reflection coefficient and radiation patterns of the fabricated antenna are measured and the results are presented and compared with the simulation.

articleTitle: 3D Non-Line-of-Sight Terahertz Imaging Using Mirror Folding
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We experimentally verify a reconstruction method for terahertz (THz) non-line-of-sight (NLoS) 3D imaging. In the THz band, common building surfaces exhibit both diffuse scattering and strong specular reflections. These properties can be combined to distinguish between line-of-sight (LoS) and NLoS objects. However, the multi-reflection propagation of THz waves in a typical scene can clutter the image with ghost objects, thus the raw image obtained from a THz imaging system lacks an accurate representation of the scene geometry. With the proposed mirror folding method, we exploit the multipath propagation to 1) correct the image from cluttering and 2) see around occlusions. To further validate the feasibility of THz NLoS imaging, we carried out an around-the-corner imaging experiment in the 270–300 GHz band achieving centimeter-scale resolution.

articleTitle: A Space-angle Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Two-Dimensional Radiative Transfer Equation with Reflective Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The propagation of radiation in the form of electromagnetic waves through a medium is affected by absorption, emission, and scattering processes. The radiative transfer equation (RTE) mathematically describes this interaction, which has a wide range of applications in such areas as heat transfer, neutron transport, atmospheric science, optical molecular imaging and some other applications. The discontinuous Galerkin (DG) finite element method (FEM) is one of the most popular grid-based numerical methods for solving the RTE due to its high order accuracy and flexibility in mesh grids. The basis functions used in the DG method are discontinuous across element interfaces; accordingly, the jump condition between interior traces of solution and the so-called numerical flux is weakly enforced on the interface boundaries. The space-angle DG methods that fully discretize the spatial and angular domain are specially suitable for the RTE, since the evolution of solution along characteristics can be strongly discontinuous when there are local radiation sources or radiation incidence coming from the boundary surface, especially the reflective ones. Previous work has proved that the space-angle DG method can be applied to solving the RTEs with high order precision in parallel with the domain decomposition (DD) and angular decomposition (AD) schemes [1]–[4]. In this paper, a parallel space-angle DG method is used to solve the steady state radiative transfer problems with the diffuse and specular reflection boundary conditions in the 2D complex geometries. Fig. 1. A schematic of the radiative intensity reflected from a surface.

articleTitle: A Robotic Antenna Alignment and Tracking System for Millimeter Wave Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the design of a sliding-correlator channel sounder for 28 GHz propagation mod-eling on the NSF POWDER testbed in Salt Lake City, UT. Beam-alignment is mechanically achieved via a fully autonomous robotic antenna tracking platform, designed using commercial off-the-shelf components. Equipped with an Apache Zookeeper/Kafka managed fault-tolerant publish-subscribe framework, we demonstrate tracking response times of 27.8 ms, in addition to superior scalability over state-of-the-art mechanical beam-steering systems. Enhanced with real-time kine-matic correction streams, our geo-positioning subsystem achieves a 3D accuracy of 17 cm, while our principal axes positioning subsystem achieves an average accuracy of 1.1º across yaw and pitch movements. Finally, by facilitating remote orchestration (via managed containers), uninhibited rotation (via encapsulation), and real-time positioning visualization (via Dash/MapBox), we exhibit a proven prototype well-suited for V2X measurements.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulation of Stochastic Scattering Loss Due to Surface Roughness in Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Ahstract― We investigate the scattering loss in optical intercon-nects comprised of dielectric slab waveguides operated at 1.54 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> source wavelength and exhibiting stochastic sidewall roughness, using the method of finite-difference time-domain (FDTD). Power degradation is numerically computed and compared against an existing analytical solution. Results show correlation between the proposed FDTD method and analytical model. A normalization is enforced based on input power to compensate for physical waveguide parameter

articleTitle: Extremely-Low Frequency (ELF) Radio Sensing of Unmanned Aerial Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper describes RF-based detection of un-manned aerial systems (UAS) without using transmit signals. The proposed scheme uses a sensitive magnetometer and digital signal processing algorithm to enable robust detection of high-torque/weig<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>t ratio rare earth magnet-based electric motors that are the enabling technology in electrical UAS. Preliminary experimental results with a 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex> receive coil show reliable detection of a small UAS at distances of several meters.

articleTitle: Low-Probability-of-Intercept/Detect (LPI/LPD) Secure Communications Using Phased-Arrays Employing Side-Lobe Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We present an approach for achieving low-probability-of-intercept (LPI) and low-probability-of-detect (LPD) secure communications. The proposed approach uses a phased-array antenna with rapid side-lobe time modulation (SLTM) capabilities. SLTM can be achieved using a conventional phased-array architecture that allows for extremely fast beam forming and shaping. We illustrate the concept using an O-slot patch antenna integrated with two high-speed RF switches for the element of the SLTM array. SLTM is achieved when switched reconfiguring within the phased-array is used to rapidly change the side-lobe shapes and directions with neglectable impact on the main lobe. By pseudorandomly and alternatively controlling the array elements at high speed, the signal radiated from SLTM array is unchanged in the main lobe direction but is covert and entirely distorted along the side-lobe directions.

articleTitle: Enabling Low-power Radiometers with Machine Learning Calibration
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Smart sensors of the future will be designed to extract maximum value information while minimizing the resources required to acquire, downlink and process data. Such intelligent instruments will reduce mission costs by avoiding taking measurements of uninteresting or unnecessary features while still capturing useful and beneficial data. However, many sensors like radiometers can make calibrated measurements only after reaching near thermal equilibrium; this requirement leads to wasted power, excess data, and delays in acquiring useful information. Furthermore, available spacecraft power and/or thermal requirements can lead to the need for power cycling a radiometer. Turning power off to an instrument stops its data acquisition but also leads to a loss of data when the instrument is powered back on until its electronics are sufficiently stable to make a calibrated measurement. As minimizing resource utilization is key to realizing future radiometer technology, in this paper, we propose the creation of a framework that uses machine learning techniques to unlock transient states of radiometers for obtaining calibrated measurements.

articleTitle: Impact of Precipitation Regimes on Deep Learning based Nowcasting Performance
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting refers to a detailed analysis and description of the current precipitation and then forecasting ahead for a period from 0 to 6 h. It plays an important role in early weather warning system and real-time decision making for disaster management and risk reduction. In the past few years, deep learning techniques have shown dramatic promise in this area. However, the performance of deep learning methods is influenced by the diversity of data and underlying precipitation microphysics. Therefore, this paper proposes a deep learning-based system for precipitation nowcasting using multi-radar observations and investigates the impact of two typical precipitation regimes on the nowcasting performance. The nowcasting problem is first transformed into an image-to-image prediction problem. The input of the model is five consecutive radar images of previous observations; the output is the predicted radar reflectivity images. Actual observations from “future” sequences are used as targets in the training stage. The system is trained using convective precipitation data and tested during both stratiform and convective precipitation events. Preliminary results show that this nowcasting system has excellent performance during convective precipitation events and a great potential to be upgraded for stratiform rain applications.

articleTitle: The Sun Radio Interferometer Space Experiment (SunRISE) Mission
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The Sun Radio Interferometer Space Experiment (SunRISE) will reveal aspects of how solar energetic particles (SEPs) are accelerated at coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and the mag-netic field topology affecting how SEPs are released into interplanetary space. SunRISE will exploit a combination of very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) techniques and a constel-lation of small space vehicles to provide spatially and temporally resolved observations of decametric-hectometric (DH, < 15 MHz) radio bursts that cannot be observed on Earth due to ionospheric absorption.

articleTitle: On-Demand Current Pulse Activation of RF Monopole Antenna Biosensor Arrays with Nitrocellulose Membranes
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Continuous glucose monitors currently on the market are expensive and uncomfortable due to their short operational lifespans of 14 days or less limited by biofouling. To address this problem, we propose a biosensor array skin patch that would increase the device functional lifetime significantly. Each sensor, based on a quarter wave monopole antenna, is housed in a PDMS well. The sensors read changes in voltage reflection coefficient (dB). Combustible nitrocellulose membranes prevent early contact of sensors with the interstitial fluid. A current pulse passed through a metal filament sufficiently disintegrated the membrane on top to allow interstitial fluid to enter thereby activating a new sensor.

articleTitle: Taylor-like Super-directive Patterns Enable Advanced Super-oscillatory Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper two types of super-directive Taylor-like antenna patterns are introduced, where the super-directivity, the first sidelobe level and the tapering rate of the sidelobes can be customized. By migrating to the spatial domain, a Taylor-like super-oscillatory point-spread function can be realized using a liquid-crystal spatial light modulator, in the form of a specialized grating, to perform advanced super-oscillatory optical imaging.

articleTitle: ACCURACy: Adaptive Calibration of CubeSat Radiometer Constellations
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Constellations of CubeSat radiometers are increasingly used in scientific applications due to their low cost and power requirements as well as their ease of deployment relative to conventional radiometer systems. However, using constellations of small CubeSats rather than conventional radiometer systems comes with additional challenges, particularly in instrument calibration, due to the sensitivity of the instrument to ambient conditions and the use of vicarious earth calibration measurements. To address these problems, we developed a novel, constellation-level calibration framework called “Adaptive Calibration of CubeSat Radiometer Constellations (ACCURACy).” ACCURACy uses machine learning algorithms to cluster CubeSat radiometers in a constellation using telemetry data. These calibration measurements and times are managed in cluster-level calibration data pools to share calibration data among other cluster members and enable frequent calibration. This paper discusses the development of the ACCURACy framework in MATLAB, along with analyses of simulations of CubeSat radiometer constellations. The performance of ACCURACy is compared to conventional intercalibration algorithms.

articleTitle: A 3D-Printed Microwave Passive Sensor Using Fully Biodegradable and Renewable Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents the feasibility of fully biodegradable and renewable materials in the fabrication of mi-crowave resonator passive sensors using additive manufacturing technology. To demonstrate this application, a microwave ring resonator sensor has been designed and fabricated. The core of sensor is a microwave ring resonator with a resonance at 4.88 GHz which is coupled through the two coupling capacitors at the input and output ports. It is demonstrated that any change in the relative permittivity of the material being sensed above the sensor produces a significant resonant frequency variation in the response of sensor. BioFila silk is used for the substrate part of the sensor. Biofila silk is characterized over an ultra-wide frequency range from 200 MHz to 20 GHZ using Keysight 85070E high performance probe. Annealed copper is used for the conductive parts of the sensor. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported passive sensor fabricated with a fully biodegradable and renewable host substrate.

articleTitle: Extending Range of Wireless Power Transfer Using a Novel Intermediate Passive Loop with Coils
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) suffers from limited range of separation between transmitter and receiver coils. We propose a novel method of using an intermediate passive wireless loop with multiple coils that allows large separation of WPT transmitter and receiver coils. Proof-of-concept results are presented using commercial Qi WPT systems where the transmitter and receiver coils were separated by 10 inches, while still providing almost identical voltage and current outputs.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Geometric Parameter Estimation of Hidden Objects in Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: A geometric parameter estimation algorithm is proposed to quantify location and size of objects hidden in stratified media. Unlike conventional ground penetrating radar images, focused near-field microwave images are reconstructed. Due to the lensing effect, primary coherent images tend to present inaccurate size of the embedded targets. However, the lensing effect could be exploited to cast shadows of the buried objects onto the rear interface. The shadow image shows the accurate size information. To quantify the location and size, the approach of spatial moments is investigated. The efficiency of the proposed geometric parameter estimation algorithm is demonstrated based on measurements of multiple targets buried in layered environments.

articleTitle: Bench Testing a System on Chip Adaptive Beamformer For GPS
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: System on chip devices have enabled miniaturization of multi-antenna wireless radios into single printed circuit board designs. This technology enables new capability for electroni-cally steerable phased array antennas. One case of interest in this paper is improving GPS reliability in heavy multi-path environments and/or in the presence of hostile spoofing agents. This paper documents a test of a 16 port digital beamformer implemented within a system on chip device. The system on chip architecture with heterogeneous FPGA + CPU signal processing is relatively compact and requires a minimal RF analog front end, suggesting a system amenable to vehicular integrations. This paper documents bench top tests of an adaptive statistical maxi-mum directivity beamformer with tone and recorded GPS inputs. The beamformer provides measured 8.9 dB of beamformer gain for GPS. These tests also show how multi-beam digital phased arrays can have viable compact implementations in system on chip devices.

articleTitle: State of the Art Transformer Enabled 2–20 GHz GaN MMIC Overview
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Ahstract- This paper presents an overview of state of the art 2 – 20 GHz GaN MMIC power amplifiers which are all fabricated on 100 μm silicon carbide using Qorvo's QGaN15 released process. Two unique two-stage amplifiers will be discussed. First, a two-stage 10 W power amplifier is presented which introduces a decade bandwidth output impedance transformer enabling substantially higher output power at lower DC operating voltage which enables substantial bandwidth and power added efficiency improvement relative to prior state of the art. Finally, a 20 W power amplifier is presented which introduces a decade bandwidth transformer-based power combiner which enables monolithic, broadband combining of core amplifiers to further push the boundaries of achievable output power.

articleTitle: DNN Enabled Real-Time Modeling of EM LWD Tool Responses in Complex Subsurface Formations
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, a fast forward modeling framework for predicting the logging-while-drilling (LWD) tool responses is presented. Unlike the traditional numerical methods based on the finite difference or finite element method, the proposed approach makes use of a deep neural network (DNN). During the offline training stage, the DNN is trained to extract the mapping from the formation parameters to tool responses. Then it can be used to predict the tool responses immediately given the formation parameters. The target application is the directional LWD operations, where the formation resistivity model has to be updated on the fly. This requires an extremely efficient forward modeling of LWD tool responses. Numerical tests are presented and results indicate the proposed method is outperforming the conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Mobile, High Temporal and Spatial Resolution FMCW Channel Sounder
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Previous studies on RF forest propagation have in-vestigated path losses and channel impulse responses as functions of range and foliage type [1]–[2]. Forests are known to be a complex channel that impact the integrity of a signal via phenomena such as fading, dispersion, and spectral broadening. These adverse effects depend on the random distribution of tree trunks, the overall density of the forest, ground reflections, and Doppler shifts resulting from swaying trees. However, these studies have traditionally used insufficient bandwidth to resolve the rich multipath characteristics of through-forest channels. Therefore, we have developed a wide band (160 MHz) frequency modulated, continuous wave mobile channel sounder capable of resolving meter-level detail of forested paths in the L-, S-, and C-Band frequencies. This paper describes the design and testing of this system, as well as presents data from a preliminary forest channel sounding.

articleTitle: A New Routine to Simulate Plasma Density Measurements from Satellites: Application to the SPORT Project
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)

authors.preferredName: Joao Pedro de Jesus Pereira Borher Jardim

abstract: In this work, we simulated plasma density measurements along prescribed satellite circular orbits, varying the inclination in relation to the geographic equator. The IRI (International Reference Ionosphere) code was used to simulate the ionosphere and the orbits were simulated using a MATLAB® code. We developed a routine to interpolate the densities along the trajectory and plot the density curves measured by the satellite over time. We show how this curve is influenced by the inclination of the orbits and also by the time when the satellite crosses the magnetic equator. It was concluded that, over the Brazilian sector, curves that pass through conjugated points along the magnetic equator during the day tend to present the two peaks corresponding to the Appleton anomaly in a pronounced way. Due to the typical declination of the magnetic field in the Brazilian sector, the inclination of the CubeSat orbit of the SPORT (Scintillation Prediction Observation Research Task) project, of 51.6°, meets this condition for descending orbits. Analyzing complete tra-jectories at inclination angles of 51.6°, it was verified that the magnetic equator crossing time significantly influences the observed peaks related to the anomaly. The simulations also showed significant differences between different orbits that pass through the equator at the same local time but in different geographic regions, showing morphological differences in the Earth's magnetic field. The methodology developed here will be used in the interpretation of the experimental results obtained from SPORT, allowing direct comparison between simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Microwave Characterization of NinjaFlex Filament Using Performance Probe for Developing 3D-Printed Wearable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper presents the microwave characterization of NinjaFlex 3D-printing filament using Keysight 85070E Perfor-mance Probe. The electromagnetic properties (dielectric constant and dielectric loss factor) of the NinjaFlex are measured from 200 MHz to 20 GHz, and its loss tangents values <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tan\delta)$</tex> are calculated accordingly. The results are compared with previously reported techniques based on ring resonator and Keysight N1501A High Temperature Dielectric Probe. To investigate the application of NinjaFlex filament for antenna manufacturing, a triangular edge-fed patch antenna is designed and simulated based on the measured electromagnetic properties. To examine the antenna's potential for wearable applications, numerical and experimental tests are conducted on its performance under structural de-formation such as bending and in proximity of human body. The reflection coefficient of the fabricated antenna are measured in flat and bent conditions and the results are presented and compared with the simulation.

articleTitle: Antarctic Firn Characterization through Wideband Microwave Radiometry
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) constellation is utilized in this study as a single multifrequency wideband radiometer to profile subsurface properties of the Antarctic firn. Initial analyses focusing on the Concordia station in Antarctica indicate that GPM brightness temperature measurements provide important information regarding the physical and thermal properties of the firn down to a few tens of meters depth from the surface. Thus, wideband microwave radiometry provides an excellent opportunity for characterizing the Antarctic firn with broad spatiotemporal coverage.

articleTitle: Magnetically Reconfigurable Band-Reject Metasurface Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper we present the design and simulation results of a magnetically reconfigurable 13×13 metasurface band-reject filter operating at 10 GHz. The tunable filter switches between all-pass and band-reject modes when heated and a magnetic field is applied. The structure consists of magnetic neodymium particles embedded in a soft polymer. Patterned copper tape is used as a conductive layer to yield the desired filtering behavior. Simulations indicate 23 to 35 dB of rejection in ideal (infinite) and 13×13 cases. This approach benefits from linearity, ease of scalability, and lack of a biasing circuit. To the knowledge of the authors, this is the first time a reconfigurable metasurface filter with magnetically actuated soft polymers is presented.

articleTitle: Matching Techniques for Microstrip Antennas in Classes Teaching Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This paper describes a procedure for determining the optimal position for a probe-fed microstrip patch antenna to achieve 50 Ohm matching. The procedure requires an initial simulation of the driving point impedance of an arbitrary probe position. Next, the impedance locus as seen on the Smith chart is rotated so that the magnitude of the reflection coefficient lies on the horizontal axis of the Smith chart. After that, one algebraic calculation is used to determine the new probe position needed for a 50 Ohm match. Such techniques give important insight for students learning matching in a classroom environment.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Parallel Plate Sinuous Antenna for Direction Finding Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: An ultra-wideband parallel plate sinuous antenna structure is proposed for direction finding application from 2 GHz to 18 GHz. In addition to direction finding, the proposed design may be used for radar systems, broadband communications, and ultra-wideband ground penetrating radar (GPR) signal processing. The structure consists of two parallel plate sinuous antennas for receive and transmit. Each antenna has an end-fire radiation pattern with a gain of 10 dB and a VSWR below 2 in the operational bandwidth. This structure can be used in a circular array for direction-finding applications. The unique property of this type of antenna is its stable radiation pattern over the entire range of frequencies. The antenna has been simulated and optimized using CST software.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Varactor Diode Modeling
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Machine learning is one tool that can be used to model circuits with complex characteristics. This paper explores the use of a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) approximation method to model and characterize tunable varactor diodes using the available information on the datasheets. The method used is easily expandable and can rapidly generate a massive amount of data points. Once properly trained, the model resulted in a highly accurate approximation of the characteristics, calculating a mean squared error for the output variables of the equivalent resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{eq})$</tex> being <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.04\times 10^{-8}$</tex> and the equivalent capacitance value for the diode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(C_{eq})$</tex> being <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.24 \times 10^{-19}$</tex>. The proposed method was validated by modeling a commercially available varactor and comparing the results with the data provided by the vendor.

articleTitle: Transitional Reversible-Jump MCMC for Subsurface Characterization
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Trans-dimensional MCMC, also known as reversible jump MCMC (RJMCMC), has been applied to geophysical inverse problems since it may generate samples from any dimensional space. However, like MCMC, RJMCMC suffers from long running time due to the sequential evaluation of the likelihood function. In this abstract, we propose the transitional RJMCMC (T-RJMCMC) algorithm that combines the parallel nature of transitional MCMC (TMCMC) and the flexibility of RJMCMC. The proposed algorithm is used to infer earth model parameters from borehole electromagnetic measurements. The experimental results show that the T-RJMCMC algorithm achieves similar, if not better results than MCMC and TMCMC, with an affordable time cost.

articleTitle: API Design for Machine-Learning-Based Automatic Synthesis of Practical Impedance Matching Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Machine-learning-based practical circuit synthesis requires data sets that consist of massive amounts of samples for the training and testing of the machine learning models. In order to generate such a large amount of samples, fast and automatic data generation methods are in demand. In this paper, we present an application programming interface (API) which, with a single Python script, can launch a massive amount of simulations in Keysight ADS, collect them, and post-process them in a machine learning environment. The proposed API can also be used to consider practical issues (e.g., parasitic effects, nonlinearity) during circuit synthesis and provide the part numbers of commercial components needed for a circuit with desired performance. To demonstrate the proposed API, it was employed in a synthesis tool of a practical 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order impedance matching circuit.

articleTitle: Object-Oriented RF Effects Simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Predicting the effect an incident electromagnetic field might have on complex electronics is a complicated and often neglected research topic in high-power electromagnetics. In this paper, we consider the advantages an object-oriented approach might have in predicting the outcome of the illumination of a device under test that we have not tested before.

articleTitle: L Band Non-Line of Sight Wave Propagation Reflected from a Tree Covered Mountainside
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: A tree covered mountainside is modelled at L Band, in order to understand the scattering mechanisms of a Non-Line of Sight (NLOS) communication channel. Due to the slope of the layer, the trees are modelled as inclined trunks with branches, needles and leaves which are azimuthally asymmetric with respect to the layer normal. This model induces polarization mixing between horizontally and vertically polarized incident waves. The effect of polarization mixing is highly dependent on the incident & scattering angles, as well as the dimensions and orientation of the individual scatterers. Ground truth measurements have been done in the White Mountains of New Hampshire to compare with the theoretical and simulation results. The main contribution to the scattering comes from the volume (direct) scatter term at L Band.

articleTitle: On the Parallel Performance of SPAI-FETD Solvers for Time-Domain Maxwell's Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We evaluate the parallel performance of the Sparse Approximate Inverse (SPAI) based Finite Element Time-Domain (FETD) method to solve time-domain Maxwell's equations. We examine the performance of the parallel computation of the SPAI matrix itself as well as the parallel speedup of the resulting SPAI-FETD simulations in a cluster machine

articleTitle: Sparse Cylindrical Arrays Based on the Low-Discrepancy Sobol Sequence Sampling
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Sparse cylindrical arrays have grating lobe issues. Aperiodic spacing can reduce the grating lobes, however random approaches typically increase the average sidelobe level in addition to creating element clumping problems. This paper explores the use of a deterministic low discrepancy quasi-random distribution. The implementation of Sobol sequence on cylindrical platforms is outlined and we present numerical results for sparse array that are capable of removing the grating lobes.

articleTitle: Two-ray Propagation Model with Random Volumetric Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The two-ray model, which is widely used in UHF propagation, is briefly overviewed. A generalization of the model to propagation in continuous random media such as atmospheric turbulence is outlined. A possible application of the two-ray model with volumetric scattering to discrete random media such as a forest or urban environment is discussed.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Patch Antenna Employing a Folded Probe Feed for Non-Linear Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this work, a set of custom folded-probe-fed patch (FPFP) antennas are designed to improve the performance of a non-linear radar (NLR) system. To improve the system performance, the antennas are designed to have high gain, relatively narrow bandwidth, good linearity, and good size, weight, and power (SWaP) performance. Two FPFP antennas are built and tested, one each for transmit (TX) and receive (RX). The VSWR and gain of the antennas are measured. The measurements show good agreement with simulated results. The antennas are then compared to a pair of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) antennas that are currently used for NLR testing. The VSWR and gain of the FPFP antennas compare favorably with those of the COTS antennas, and suggest improved NLR performance. The performance of a NLR system using the two sets of antennas is evaluated. By replacing the COTS antennas with the FPFP antennas, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvements as high as 20 dB are demonstrated. Lastly, the two FPFP antennas are integrated into a single compact, dual-band design.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna using a Proximity-Coupled Sunflower-Shaped Patch
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, a switched-beam radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna (RPRA) is presented using a proximity-coupled patch with parasitic elements. The proposed antenna, called the Sunflower RPRA for its physical resemblance, has multiple pattern states selected by RF switches. The proposed two-board design uses a circular patch along with eight pedal-shaped peripheral parasitic elements connected via switches. The antenna directs the beam to an oblique elevation angle of 30° relative to the patch-normal, while the azimuth direction can be controlled in steps of 45° based on the state of the switches. Simulation results show that the antenna is impedance matched in all states (< −10 dB) and that the gain in each directional state is 5.7 dBi at 2.6 GHz. In addition, there is an omnidirectional state with a 3.25 dBi gain across all azimuth angles.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Field Solution for a Point Source Near a Complex Transformation Optics Flat Lens
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We study the time-domain field produced by a scalar point source near a flat lens (metamaterial slab) designed from complex transformation optics (CTO) principles. Such a lens can be used to launch Gaussian beams from points sources placed next to it. We provide closed-form analytical expressions and examine in particular the behavior of the solution in the limit of small gain.

articleTitle: SuperDARN Observations of STEVE USNC-URSI National Radio Science Meeting
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In situ spacecraft observations of STEVE (Strong Thermal Emission Velocity Enhancement) have confirmed that the phenomena are an intense SAID (SubAuroral Ion Drift). These observations tell us that STEVE is typically an extremely narrow channel (of the order of 20 km) of zonal ion flows (of the order of 5 km/s) that is collocated with a minimum in the sub-auroral trough meridional plasma density profile and extremely enhanced electron temperatures (of the order of 7000 K). Statistics derived from all sky imager data of STEVE shows that it typically occurs approximately one hour after substorm onset and has a lifetime of the order of one hour. The mechanism that produces STEVE's famous mauve optical emission which has captivated the citizen science community and – more recently – the “traditional” science community remains elusive along with the evolution of the phenomena from start to finish. Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN) High Frequency (HF) radars have been used for several years to study SAID and may provide a way of studying the evolution of STEVE events, including when its optical signature is too dim to observe with an imager.

articleTitle: Technology Maturation for Cloud Ice Radiometers
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Global measurements of ice in clouds, both the amount and particle size distribution, are critically needed to reduce uncertainties in global climate models. The retrieval of this information is best achieved with a range of receiver channels across the submillimeter wave range. Advancement of low noise Indium Phosphide (InP) MMIC amplifier technology to 25-nm gate length enabled us to develop miniature submillimeter-wave receivers for a CubeSat scale instrument that achieves 6 km spatial resolution. We developed the 25-nm InP MMICs and radiometer receivers for 240, 310, 380, 670 GHz. The 25-nm InP MMIC technology was thermal vacuum tested to reduce risk for future space mission.

articleTitle: Adaptive Radio Frequency Interference Cancellation for Radio Science Observatories
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Spectrum coexistence is a major challenge facing radio science in the modern era. Scientific use of the radio spectrum aids in the study of earth's atmosphere, geospace, solar system, and the larger astronomical universe. To enable such fundamental research, scientific instruments span wide bandwidths and have high levels of sensitivity. They actively transmit in the licensed bandwidth and passively observe frequencies within and well outside the allocation. Proliferation of radio frequency (RF) systems pose interference challenges that limit the performance of radio science observatories.

articleTitle: Impacts of WSR-88D Supplemental Lower Elevation Angles on Quantitative Precipitation Estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: The standard operations of Weather Surveillance Radar − 1988 Doppler (WSR-88D) limit the lowest radar scan elevation angle to 0.5°. However, due to the curvature of the Earth and blockages induced by complex terrains, more than 70% of the atmosphere below 1km above ground level is misdetected. Recently, the National Weather Service (NWS) has lowered the lowest radar scan elevation angle from 0.5° to 0° to enhance near surface measurements. Using the KMUX radar deployed in northern California as an example, this study quantifies the impacts of radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) brought by the supplemental lower elevation angles. In addition, raindrop size distributions (DSD) measured by a disdrometer deployed in Santa Clara, California are used to investigate local DSD characteristics and derive radar rainfall relations for local applications in northern California. The newly developed radar rainfall algorithms are applied to both 0° and 0.5° observations of KMUX radar and the derived radar QPE are compared with rainfall measurements from several rain gauges. The results show that the supplemental low elevation scans can substantially improve radar quantitative precipitation estimation, especially during shallow precipitation events.

articleTitle: Circuit Models for Electrically-Small Time-Varying Spherical Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Time-variation is one method to contravene the assumptions used in deriving the Chu limit, which constrains the bandwidth of electrically-small antennas. Here, circuit models for electrically-small, time-varying, resonant scatterers are developed. The method leads to physical, frequency independent values for the reactive components within the circuit, and provides a natural formulation with which to analyze time-varying scatterers and antennas.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Exceptional Degeneracy in Coupled Transmission Lines With Balanced Gain and loss
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We proposed a highly sensitive circuit scheme based on an exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD) using two finite-length coupled transmission lines terminated on balanced gain and loss. EPD is a point in a system's parameter space in which two or more eigenmodes coalesce in both their resonance frequency and eigenvectors into a single degenerate eigenmode by varying the system's parameter. We demonstrate that two PT-symmetric finite-length coupled transmission lines (CTLs), can generate an EPD at a desired frequency. We find the EPDs in this circuit and the bifurcation diagram that exhibits the ultra-sensitivity behavior to the system's perturbations. The very high sensitivity induced by an EPD can be used to conceive a new generation of high-sensitive sensors.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of an Efficient Neural Network Model for Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a compact, efficient fully-connected neural network (FCNN) model is presented which can track maximum power point of a radio frequency (RF) based energy harvesting system. The hyperparameters of the FCNN model have been tuned to obtain optimal accuracy rate of nearly 78% and have been optimized to ensure compact design solution in miniaturized CMOS circuits. A two-hidden layer FCNN model was trained to optimize the binary cross entropy loss function. To prevent the FCNN model from overfitting, ADAM optimizer was used during the training phase. Weights and biases extracted from the best learned FCNN model were implemented into digital hardware. The application-specific trained neural network model embedded in hardware platform requires minimal resources which are significantly less compared to commercially available hardware accelerators. In future, the FCNN model can be integrated into a standard system-on-chip platform for developing RF energy harvester.

articleTitle: Using Anatomical Body Models to Simulate Antenna-Impregnated Fabrics that Monitor Child Height
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Routine child height monitoring is crucial in the detection and treatment plan identification for diverse health conditions. Nevertheless, height measurements for several children are currently sparse and inaccurate. To overcome this limitation, we previously reported an antenna impregnated fabric that can monitor height of a child lying upon it. Our proof-of-concept design was validated for a rectangular box used to simulate the child's body. In this work, we take a major step forward and validate the design for an anatomical child model in Altair Feko. Simulation results show that height can be accurately retrieved at 2 cm resolution and provide a path to further improving resolution in the future. The design can ultimately be integrated into bed sheets or mats for easy and routine monitoring of child height in non-clinical settings.

articleTitle: Prior Knowledge based Inverse Parametric Modeling of UWB Band-Notched Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We have developed a prior knowledge input-based artificial neural network model. The prior knowledge has been incorporated into the model using trained multilayer perceptron network. The proposed model has been validated by designing an f-shaped UWB antenna loaded with electromagnetic bandgap structure and rectangular split ring resonator.

articleTitle: Sparse Circular Aperture Arrays Based on Poisson Disk Sampling
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Sparse antenna arrays are effective at reducing array cost, but their design is challenging due to the large element spacings causing grating lobes. Aperiodic element spacing can remove the grating lobes, but random element positions increase the sidelobe levels and cluster some of the elements too close together. This paper explores the use of nonuniform element spacing based on Poisson-disk sampling. Array pattern results are presented for planar arrays with circular apertures with element spacings larger than one wavelength and we show that this approach is capable of removing the grating lobes and reducing the sidelobe level while keeping the elements from being too close together.

articleTitle: A High-Power-Capable, Electronically-Reconfigurable, Phased-Array Unit Cell with 1-Bit Phase Quantization and 3:1 Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: An ultra-wideband, electronically reconfigurable polarization rotating (PR) unit cell with high-power handling capability and 1-blt phase quantization is designed and simulated for high-power phased array applications. The unit cell uses a PR element embedded in a double ridge waveguide environment to achieve a nearly 3:1 bandwidth (4.1-12 GHz) with a relatively low complexity. The PR structure uses two high-power-capable PIN diodes to achieve electronic switching under high power conditions. Simulation results show that the unit cell has 177°±2° phase difference between the two modes over a 3:1 bandwidth with a maximum insertion loss of 1 dB. Multiphysics simulations suggest that a dynamic phased array using such unit cells can handle an average power level exceeding 45 kW/m2 (26 W continuous wave power per unit cell) across the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: Towards E-band Wavelength: 3D Printed Gaussian Corrugated Horn for Cassegrain Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Two Gaussian profile conical horn antennas for use within the E-band spectrum are presented. The proposed conical horn antenna is designed in three segments: Mode converter, phasing and profiled sections. These two horns with Cos n-like radiation patterns as Cassegrain antenna illuminators are analyzed to have high efficiency over the E-band (60-100GHz). Simulations show reasonable results, therefore allowing for reliable predictability. A couple of printing technologies and metal materials to realize proposed designs are analyzed with material characterizations throughout simulations, namely selective laser melting (SLM) using Cu-15Sn material and binder sintering on 316L stainless with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.79 \mu \mathrm{m}, 12.79 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> surface roughness, respectively. The slot-to-ridge width ratio for both designs is fixed to 4: 1 ratio, with a pitch of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> at 100 GHz. The provided horn antennas' impedance bandwidth (|S11| < −24 dB) covers the whole intended operational band for both E- and D spectrum. The realized in-band gain for the E-band antennas is higher than 22.14 and 22, respectively.

articleTitle: A High-Power UHF Antenna with Logarithmic Spiral Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: A wideband dual-arm logarithmic spiral antenna is fabricated for wideband applications from 500 MHz to 1000 MHz. The proposed design may be used for broadband communications, and wideband ground penetrating radar (GPR). The structure consists of a cavity, a balun, an impedance transformer, and planar antenna. The antenna has an end-fire radiation pattern with a gain of 7 dB and a VSWR below 2 in the operational bandwidth. This structure can be used in a circular array for GPR applications. The unique property of this type of antenna is its stable radiation pattern over the entire range of frequencies. The antenna has been simulated with CST software and fabricated. There is a good agreement between the simulation and measurement results

articleTitle: Inverse-design of Advanced Short Backfire Antennas with 100% Aperture Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: First introduced decades ago, the Short-Backfire Antenna (SBFA) has proven to be a well-defined, reliable, and rugged radiator often selected for use in harsh environments requiring gain greater than 15 dBi. In this report, we present the optimization of a circular Advanced Short Backfire Antenna (A-SBF A) which has been designed for dual-band operation with remarkably high aperture efficiency over a range of different aperture sizes. In contrast to the hard-EM SBFA, anisotropic, dispersive metasurfaces line the cavity walls of the circular A-SBF A and prove integral to achieving 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> aperture efficiency at the two frequency bands for diameters spanning a range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1.0\lambda_{0}}$</tex> up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2.13\lambda_{0}}$</tex>. We present an inverse-design methodology used to optimize such high-performing A-SBFA antennas, and the pursuant results. In addition, we draw a comparison between the circular A-SBFA and traditional high-efficiency short horn antennas, which is illustrative of the great impact of the circular A-SBFA.

articleTitle: Exceptional Point of Degeneracy as a Desirable Point of Operation for Oscillator With Discrete Nonlinear Gain and Radiating Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: An oscillator made of a periodic waveguide comprising of uniform lossless segments with discrete nonlinear gain and radiating resistive elements prefers to operate at exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD). The steady-state regime is an EPD with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> phase shift between unit cells, for various choices of small signal gain of the nonlinear elements and number of unit cells. We demonstrated this fact by monitoring both current and voltage across each nonlinear gain element and finding its effective admittance at the oscillating frequency and checking the degeneracy of the eigenmodes at such point. The EPD studied here is very promising for many applications that incorporate discrete distributed coherent sources and radiation-loss elements. Operating in the vicinity of such special degeneracy conditions may lead to potential performance enhancement in the various microwave, THz and optical systems with distributed gain and radiation, paving the way for a new class of active integrated antenna arrays and radiating laser arrays.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction of Miniaturized MM-wave ME-dipole Antennas using SRR Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of Split Ring Resonator (SRR) loading on mutual coupling reduction of Magneto Electric (ME)-dipole antennas fed through printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) is presented for millimeter-wave 5G applications. A miniaturized ME-dipole antenna with a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 27 to 37 GHz and a peak gain of 10 dBi at 33 GHz is designed as the elementary antenna. As a proof of concept, a two-port ME-dipole antenna with half-wavelength inter-element spacing is loaded with a single SRR layer in the elevation plane. The simulated results demonstrate that the SRR superstrate reduces the mutual coupling by up to 12 dB while maintaining the impedance bandwidth of the antenna. Moreover, the realized gain of the antenna is improved in the upper bandwidth by up to 2.4 dBi due to the SRR's phase compensation on the antenna aperture.

articleTitle: Understanding the Far-Field Properties of Orbital Angular Momentum Beams through the Antenna Aperture Field Method
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: This work aims to provide insight into the far-field properties of orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams. Semi-analytical expressions for the far field of a general cylindrically-symmetric OAM aperture field are derived using the antenna aperture field method. The far-field properties of a circularly-polarized OAM carrying fields are considered. In particular, we derive analytical expression for the minimum theoretically achievable AR of a circularly-polarized OAM beam. For a common OAM-carrier aperture field distribution, i.e., the Laguerre-Gaussian distribution, analytical expressions of the fields are obtained in closed forms. The equations obtained in this paper show excellent agreement with predictions obtained from full-wave simulations. The derived analytical and semi-analytical formulas can potentially guide the design of OAM communication systems.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Using Lightweight Carbon-Epoxy Composites as a Microstrip Patch Antenna Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: Microstrip patch antenna substrates are commonly made of metal; this is an investigation on advantages for substitution of metal substrates with Carbon Fiber Reinforced Composites (CFRCs). The composite substrate made of carbon fiber reinforced material is investigated for its mechanical properties such as the flexural modulus and flexural strength which are determined to be 112.22GPa and 1461.27MPa respectively, from a three-point bending test. The bending modulus obtained from ABAQUS simulation is 118.51GPa. The results demonstrate adequate mechanical properties for a lower weight compared to conventional metal substrates. Moreover, manipulation of the direction of carbon fibers could help with adjusting certain properties such as the resulting current density affecting the scatter parameter, bandwidth, and antenna gain.

articleTitle: Enhanced Sensitivity of Gyrator-based Circuit at Exceptional Point Composed of Unstable Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 United States National Committee of URSI National Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI NRSM)
abstract: We show the enhanced sensitivity to perturbations of a circuit comprising two unstable resonators coupled via a gyrator in the vicinity of the exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD) with purely real eigenfrequency. Each resonator includes a negative capacitance, showing purely imaginary resonance frequency when not coupled via the gyrator. When applying an external perturbation to the circuit, we confirm that the eigenfrequencies of the circuit follow the typical second-order EPD square-root dependence on perturbation, leading to possible sensor applications. We analyze the effect of losses in the resonators that lead to instability. The very high sensitivity induced by an EPD paves the way to realize a new generation of high-sensitive sensors to measure small physical or chemical perturbations.
